import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Congruences $a(n+k) \equiv a(n) \pmod k$ for hypergeometric values ${}_2F_1(n, -n; ; -1)$

a: $a(n) = \text{hypergeometric}([n, -n], [], -1)$.
This is equivalent to the combinatorial sum:
$$a(n) = \sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k} \binom{n+k-1}{k} k!$$
The expression uses $\mathbb{N}$ arithmetic throughout, safely handling
the subtraction via `Nat.pred`.

*References:*
- [A278070](https://oeis.org/A278070)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

namespace OeisA278070


open Nat Finset

/--
a: $a(n) = \text{hypergeometric}([n, -n], [], -1)$.
This is equivalent to the combinatorial sum:
$$a(n) = \sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k} \binom{n+k-1}{k} k!$$
The expression uses $\mathbb{N}$ arithmetic throughout, safely handling
the subtraction via `Nat.pred`.
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.range (n + 1)).sum fun k =>
    (n.choose k) * ((n + k).pred.choose k) * (k.factorial)


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 2 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 11 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 106 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 1457 := by rfl


/--
Conjecture: $a(n+k) \equiv a(n) \pmod{k}$ for all $n$ and $k$. - _Peter Bala_, Mar 12 2023

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/278070.wip.lean#L68"]
theorem a_modeq : ∀ (n k : ℕ), Nat.ModEq k (a (n + k)) (a n) := by
    sorry

end OeisA278070

findings.description: The module title at line 20 writes `{}_2F_1(n, -n; ; -1)`, but the sequence has two upper parameters and no lower parameters, so it is a `{}_2F_0` value. The definition `OeisA278070.a`, its docstring, and the congruence theorem are correct; only the special-function notation in the title is wrong.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A278070 defines `a(n) = hypergeometric([n, -n], [], -1)` and gives Mathematica code `HypergeometricPFQ[{n, -n}, {}, -1]` (https://oeis.org/A278070, read through its official OEIS data mirror). DLMF equation 16.2.1 specifies that the subscript q in pFq counts lower parameters: https://dlmf.nist.gov/16.2.E1.tex.
findings.suggested_fix: Change `{}_2F_1(n, -n; ; -1)` to `{}_2F_0(n, -n; ; -1)` in the module title. No Lean declaration needs changing.

reformulations.difference: The sequence is implemented as a finite natural-number binomial sum using `Nat.pred`, rather than directly as the hypergeometric function appearing in the OEIS sequence name.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Writing (x)_j for the rising factorial, the hypergeometric term (n)_j(-n)_j(-1)^j/j! equals binom(n,j) binom(n+j-1,j) j!. Terms with j>n vanish. At n=j=0, the term is 1, and replacing the upper binomial argument -1 by Nat.pred 0 = 0 preserves binom(-1,0)=binom(0,0)=1. OEIS explicitly supplies the same finite-sum formula. In /workspace/review/hypergeometric.lean, I proved the term identity using Mathlib Pochhammer polynomials, vanishing beyond n, the summed identity, and an explicit equivalence of the corresponding congruence statements, without sorry.

reformulations.difference: Lean makes the modular-congruence assertion meaningful also at modulus k=0, rather than requiring the usual positive-modulus restriction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For k=0, n+k=n, so the additional assertion is reflexivity. Thus, for any sequence b : ℕ → ℕ, the all-natural-moduli statement is equivalent to the statement restricted to k>0. This generic equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean; no property of a or unproved conjecture was used.

review.notes: All seven declarations were checked. The first 13 computed terms match the OEIS b-file, and all 961 congruence tests with 0 ≤ n,k ≤ 30 passed. The solved tag agrees with OEIS's May 31, 2026 proof announcement. The cited proof was replayed in scratch with compatibility-only changes (updated import, renamed binomial identity, elaboration setting, and heartbeat limit); its statement matches a_modeq definitionally, and #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. OEIS's main HTML page was blocked, so its official data mirror was used. No repository files were edited.
